subject: English
topic: Direct and Indirect Narration — Advanced Conversion (W11 B1)

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'She said, "I am going to the market."'

options.option_text: She said that she is going to the market.
She said that she was going to the market.
She said that I was going to the market.
She told that she was going to the market.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rules applied: (1) 'said' (past) → tense backshifts: 'am going' → 'was going'. (2) First person 'I' changes to 'she' (matches the reporting subject). (3) Quotation marks and comma removed; 'that' introduced. (4) 'said' (without object) remains 'said', NOT 'told' — 'told' requires an object ('told me/him'). Trap: A = no backshift; C = 'I' not changed to 'she'; D = 'told that' wrong ('told' needs an indirect object before 'that').

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'He asked me, "Where do you live?"'

options.option_text: He asked me where do I live.
He asked me where I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Rules for WH-question in indirect speech: (1) Remove question mark; (2) Change question word order to normal statement order (not inverted): 'where do you live' → 'where I lived'; (3) 'you' → 'I' (object 'me' is the person spoken to); (4) 'do you live' backshifts to 'I lived'. Trap: A and D use inverted word order ('do I live', 'did I live') — wrong for indirect speech which uses statement order; B fails to backshift ('live' not 'lived').

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'The teacher said, "Sit down and be quiet."'

options.option_text: The teacher said to sit down and be quiet.
The teacher said that sit down and be quiet.
The teacher ordered them to sit down and be quiet.
The teacher told that they sit down and be quiet.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Imperatives in indirect speech: (1) The reporting verb changes to 'ordered', 'requested', 'told', 'asked', or 'commanded' depending on tone; (2) 'Sit down' → 'to sit down' (infinitive form); (3) Subject for the imperative (implicit 'you') becomes the implied audience ('them'). 'Ordered them to sit down and be quiet' = correct form for an imperative command. Trap: A omits the audience object ('said to sit' is informal/wrong in formal grammar); B uses 'that' before an imperative — wrong construction; D uses 'told that' with a finite clause instead of infinitive.

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'She said, "I have never seen such a beautiful painting."'

options.option_text: She said that she had never seen such a beautiful painting.
She said that she has never seen such a beautiful painting.
She said that I had never seen such a beautiful painting.
She exclaimed that she had never seen such a beautiful painting.

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Have never seen' = Present Perfect → backshifts to 'had never seen' (Past Perfect). 'I' → 'she'. 'Said' is retained (no object = use 'said', not 'told'). The sentence is a statement (not an exclamation despite emotional content), so 'said' is the correct reporting verb. Trap: B keeps 'has never seen' without backshift; C keeps 'I' unchanged; D = 'exclaimed' is used for exclamatory sentences (with 'what a...!' or 'how...!'), not this type of emphatic statement.

questions.stem:
Convert to Direct Speech:
'Raman told me that he would finish the work the next day.'

options.option_text: Raman said to me, "I will finish the work tomorrow."
Raman said to me, "I will finish the work the next day."
Raman told me, "He will finish the work tomorrow."
Raman said to me, "I would finish the work tomorrow."

questions.explanation: A is correct. Rules for converting indirect to direct: (1) 'would finish' → 'will finish' (reverse backshift); (2) 'the next day' → 'tomorrow' (reverse time reference change); (3) 'he' → 'I' (first person in direct speech); (4) 'told me' → 'said to me' + quotation marks. Trap: B keeps 'the next day' instead of reverting to 'tomorrow'; C keeps 'he' instead of changing to 'I'; D keeps 'would' in the direct speech (direct speech must use the original tense 'will', not the backshifted 'would').

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'The doctor said to the patient, "Take this medicine twice daily."'

options.option_text: The doctor told the patient to take the medicine twice daily.
The doctor said to the patient that take this medicine twice daily.
The doctor told the patient that he should take the medicine twice daily.
The doctor advised the patient that you should take medicine twice daily.

questions.explanation: A is correct. For an imperative (instruction): reporting verb = told/ordered/asked/advised + object + to + infinitive. 'Take this medicine' → 'to take the medicine' (article change: 'this' → 'the'). 'The doctor TOLD the patient TO TAKE the medicine twice daily.' Trap: B uses 'said to the patient that' + imperative (wrong — 'that' introduces a finite clause, not an imperative); C is also valid ('should take') but A is more direct and precise; D switches 'advised' correctly but then uses 'you' (wrong — reported speech drops second person).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'He said, "Can you lend me some money?"'

options.option_text: He asked if I can lend him some money.
He asked me if I could lend him some money.
He asked if can I lend him some money.
He asked whether I could lend him some money.

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Can you...' = yes/no question → indirect: 'if/whether' + statement order. 'Can' backshifts to 'could'. 'You' → 'I' (the person being asked). 'Me' → 'him'. 'He asked me if I could lend him some money.' Note: D ('whether') is also grammatically correct — both 'if' and 'whether' can introduce indirect yes/no questions. However, B specifies 'asked me' (with indirect object) which is more complete and unambiguous as the answer. Trap: A keeps 'can' without backshift; C uses inverted question order ('can I') which is wrong in indirect speech.

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'The principal said, "Honesty is the best policy."'

options.option_text: The principal said that honesty was the best policy.
The principal said that honesty had been the best policy.
The principal said that honesty is the best policy.
The principal told that honesty was the best policy.

questions.explanation: C is correct. EXCEPTION: Universal truths, proverbs, and general facts do NOT backshift in indirect speech. 'Honesty is the best policy' is a proverb/universal truth — it remains in Present Simple ('is'), even when the reporting verb is past ('said'). 'The principal said that honesty IS the best policy.' Trap: A backshifts to 'was' — wrong for universal truths; B over-backshifts to 'had been' (past perfect) — completely wrong; D uses 'told that' without object — wrong ('told' needs an object).

questions.stem:
Convert to Indirect Speech:
'She exclaimed, "What a beautiful dress!"'

options.option_text: She exclaimed what a beautiful dress it was.
She exclaimed that it was a very beautiful dress.
She said what a beautiful dress it was.
She exclaimed that the dress was very beautiful.

questions.explanation: B is correct. For exclamatory sentences: (1) Reporting verb = 'exclaimed'; (2) 'What a beautiful ___' → 'that it was a very beautiful ___' (the superlative exclamatory is converted to 'very' + adjective form in a 'that' clause). 'She exclaimed that it was a VERY beautiful dress.' Trap: A keeps the exclamatory form after 'exclaimed' — wrong (it should become a 'that' clause); C uses 'said' instead of 'exclaimed'; D is close but changes the subject ('the dress was' instead of 'it was a dress') — the transformation should preserve 'it was a [adjective] [noun]' structure.

questions.stem:
Identify the INCORRECT conversion of direct to indirect speech:
(A) 'He said, "I will come tomorrow."' → 'He said that he would come the next day.'
(B) 'She said, "I am happy."' → 'She said that she was happy.'
(C) 'He said, "I went there yesterday."' → 'He said that he had gone there the previous day.'
(D) 'She said, "I can do it."' → 'She said that she can do it.'

options.option_text: A
B
C
D

questions.explanation: D is the incorrect conversion. 'Can' must backshift to 'could' in indirect speech. Correct indirect: 'She said that she COULD do it.' — not 'can'. A is correct: 'will' → 'would', 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'. B is correct: 'am' → 'was'. C is correct: 'went' (simple past) → 'had gone' (past perfect), 'yesterday' → 'the previous day'. Only D fails to apply the modal backshift (can → could).
